name: Chelal
overview: Chelal is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Pahath-moab, noted specifically for having married a foreign wife. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture provides limited information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Chelal means 'perfection' or 'completeness.' It is a proper name mentioned in Ezra 10:30, though it was not given by God. This meaning may reflect a Hebrew linguistic root but does not imply any divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Chelal is explicitly recorded as a descendant of Pahath-moab. Other than this lineage, Scripture does not provide further family relationships or connections beyond his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Chelal's mention in Ezra 10:30 highlights the post-exilic concern for Israelite purity in marriage, as he is listed among those who had married foreign wives. His inclusion underscores the broader narrative of the community's efforts to separate from foreign influences and renew covenant faithfulness. Though a minor figure, Chelal represents the challenges faced by the returning exiles in maintaining holiness according to God's standards.
